source_title: Mule Entering Barn Mechanical Coin Bank
desc_src: Cast iron mechanical bank depicting a mule, dog and barn.To make a deposit, a coin is placed between the mule's hind legs; pushing the lever will cause the mule to kick its legs and transfer the coin into the barn. At the same time, the dog will emerge from the barn. Manufactured by the J and E Stevens Company circa 1880. Title: Mule Entering Barn Mechanical Coin Bank

source_title: Low Waterfall in a Wooded Landscape with a Dead Beech Tree
desc_src: Jutting from a dune in the foreground, the massive silvery trunk of a dead tree leads the eye across a waterfall and toward a distant sunlit field where travelers and a dog traverse a sandy path. Partly masked by trees, a ruined building is turned gold by the sun. In Jacob van Ruisdael’s landscapes, dead trees, waterfalls, and ruined buildings were visual expressions of the passage of time. Ruisdael devoted equal attention to the cloud-filled skies looming above the land, creating dramatic patterns of light and shadow and revealing the unseen movements of the wind.

source_title: Boys Stealing Watermelons Mechanical Coin Bank
desc_src: Cast iron mechanical bank. Depicts two African American boys stealing watermelons from a field guarded by a dog in a doghouse. To make a deposit, a coin is placed in the slot on top of the dog house. Pushing a lever moves the dog out of the house allowing the coin to fall. The action also animates the boys' arms. Manufactured by the Kyser and Rex Company from 1885 to 1895. Title: Boys Stealing Watermelons Mechanical Coin Bank

In 1903, he moved to Paris where he met poet Guillaume Apollinaire and artists Georges Braque and Pablo Picasso. He then began experimenting with Cubism. When posed in this powerful and exuberant manner, the image of Hanuman stood at the top of a standard. As the son of the wind god and the most powerful of the primeval forest-dwellers, who are depicted with the head and tail of a monkey and the body of a man, Hanuman as an emblem spelled success in battle.

Cast iron mechanical bank in the shape of a house and dog. To deposit a coin, the dog is pulled back and the coin placed on a platter in its mouth. Raising the dog's tail releases the action, causing the dog to shoot forward, depositing the coin in the house. Manufactured by the H.L. Judd Company circa 1880. Title: Gem Mechanical Coin Bank
Cast iron bank depicting a cat on top of a hatching egg. Coin slot is on top of the cat's back. When a coin is deposited the hatching chicken's head moves. Title: Tabby Mechanical Coin Bank

Cast iron mechanical bank in the shape of a cabin with a African American man at the door. To deposit money you must place a coin on the roof and pull the broom handle on the side of the cabin. The man will then flip up and kick the coin into the bank. Manufactured by the J and E Stevens Company circa 1885. Title: Cabin Mechanical Coin Bank

An x-ray far-field interferometer using only phase gratings is based on the phase moiré effect. The mid grating forms Fourier images of the first grating. These images beat with the 3rd grating to produce broad moiré fringes on the detector at the appropriate distance. Phase shifts and de-coherence of the wavefront by the object cause fringe shifts and attenuation of the fringe contrast.

An x-ray far-field interferometer using only phase gratings is based on the phase moire effect. The mid grating forms Fourier images of the first grating. These images beat with the 3rd grating to produce broad moire fringes on the detector at the appropriate distance. Phase shifts and de-coherence of the wavefront by the object cause fringe shifts and attenuation of the fringe contrast.
